query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for jet-turbine applications, what single intervention could improve high-temperature mechanical capability while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its mechanism, the expected improvement relative to a relevant baseline, the temperature and loading conditions under which it should hold, supporting evidence from prior studies, and a decisive experiment with a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of boron as a grain refiner and precipitate former will improve the high-temperature mechanical capability of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) while limiting density and preserving room-temperature performance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast refractory high-entropy alloy with a nominal composition of CoCrFeMnNi
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5 wt% boron to the alloy melt before casting
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 20°C to 1000°C, loading conditions: tensile stress up to 500 MPa
generation.structural_mediator: Boron-induced grain refinement and precipitation of boride phases
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary strengthening and precipitation hardening due to boride formation, which enhances high-temperature strength and creep resistance without significantly compromising room-temperature ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: 20% increase in yield strength at 800°C and 15% reduction in density compared to the baseline alloy without boron addition
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement may vary depending on the specific alloy composition, processing conditions, and the resulting microstructure. The boron addition might also introduce brittleness at lower temperatures, which needs to be evaluated.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of boron-modified and unmodified RHEAs at room temperature and 800°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength of the boron-modified alloy at 800°C is not at least 10% higher than that of the baseline alloy, or if the room-temperature ductility (elongation at break) decreases by more than 20%, the hypothesis is falsified.
